summary: U.L. Space developed a graphic view for the NASA databased data. The idea was to provide an easy and visual way to comprehend the changes like melted ice, forestal wildfire or global warming.
details:
Earth-Time is an interactive, bilingual web experience that helps people explore how our planet changes over time. Users select wildfires, sea ice, volcanic activity, or global temperature and watch NASA data visualized on a rotating 3D Earth as the timeline advances. The project uses NASA FIRMS VIIRS, Worldview/GIBS AMSR2, EONET, and GISTEMP/LOTI data.

The project was built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WebGL, and WebXR and Codex.

Earth-Time was designed for desktop, mobile and VR headsets. It combines scientific information with an immersive interface to make climate and environmental change more engaging and accessible. Our team considered data sources, time coverage, clear explanations of what each indicator represents, and proper audio credits, so the experience encourages curiosity without implying that derived visual indicators are direct measurements.
